title: Merging paginated feed sources behind one interface
name: Merged feed paginator

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how MergedFeed implements the FeedSource-style pagination contract (cursor handling, ordering, and termination)? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
On page 1 (limit 10), source A returns 10 items and source B returns 10 items, all newer from A. What happens to B's 10 items?
choices: They are dropped, because only 10 items fit on the page
They are refetched from source B on the next call
They are returned on page 1 by truncating A's items
They are carried in the encoded cursor and merged first on the next page

questions.prompt: What is a consequence of returning the full SourceState (including buffered items) inside the cursor?
choices: The cursor string can grow to roughly the number of sources times limit items
Clients can no longer request page 1 again
Sources must be stateful and remember viewer cursors server-side
Items can appear twice across pages

questions.prompt: A client sends a cursor produced before a new source with key "trending" was added to the configuration. What does fetchPage do?
choices: Starts "trending" from its first page and continues the others
Throws a RangeError because the cursor lacks an entry for "trending"
Ignores the cursor and returns page 1
Returns an empty page with nextCursor null
